questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a Fundamental Right under the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4) Right to Property**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Right to Property** was originally a Fundamental Right under Article 31 of the Constitution of India.
 
• It was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, and made a **legal right** under Article 300A.
 
• Fundamental Rights are guaranteed under Part III of the Constitution, but the Right to Property is not included in this category anymore.
 
• The Right to Property, as a legal right, ensures that no person shall be deprived of their property except by the authority of law.
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, a legal right under Article 300A is not enforceable directly in the Supreme Court under Article 32.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights in India:**

 
 
• There are six Fundamental Rights enshrined in the Indian Constitution, which are essential for the development of individuals and protecting them from state encroachment.
 
• These include the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22), Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24), Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28), Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30), and Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32).
 
 
 
• **Legal Rights vs. Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• Legal rights are granted by ordinary laws and can be amended or repealed by the legislature, whereas Fundamental Rights are enshrined in the Constitution and are protected from legislative encroachment.
 
• Fundamental Rights are enforceable by the Supreme Court under Article 32, but legal rights are enforceable in lower courts.
 
 
 
• **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978:**
 
 
• This amendment abolished the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right and reclassified it as a constitutional legal right under Article 300A.
 
• The amendment was introduced to reduce conflicts between the state and individuals over property acquisition for public purposes.
 
 
 
• **Right to Property under Article 300A:**
 
 
• It ensures that no person shall be deprived of their property except by the authority of law, providing protection against arbitrary dispossession.
 
• However, since it is not a Fundamental Right, violations cannot be directly challenged in the Supreme Court under Article 32.

questions.question: The Joint Sitting of the parliament is governed by the rules of ___________

options.text: Special Rules mentioned by the Cabinet

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1. Lok Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 108** of the Indian Constitution provides for a Joint Sitting of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) to resolve disagreements on legislative matters.
 
• The **Speaker of the Lok Sabha** presides over the Joint Sitting, as explicitly mentioned in the Constitution. This is irrespective of whether the bill originated in the Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha.
 
• In the Speaker’s absence, the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides. If both are unavailable, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha may preside. *Hence, Option 1 is correct.*
 
• The rules of procedure of the Lok Sabha govern the conduct of the Joint Sitting. These rules ensure smooth functioning and decision-making during such sessions.
 
• The Joint Sitting provision is used sparingly and is considered a mechanism to address legislative deadlocks in the Indian parliamentary system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 108 of the Constitution:**

 
 
• This article empowers the President of India to summon a Joint Sitting of Parliament to resolve disagreements between the two Houses on a bill.
 
• A Joint Sitting is convened when one House passes a bill, and the other House either rejects it, proposes amendments not agreeable to the originating House, or fails to take any action within six months.
 
 
 
• **Role of Lok Sabha and Speaker:**
 
 
• As the Lok Sabha represents the majority of elected representatives, its Speaker presides over the Joint Sitting to ensure democratic representation in decision-making.
 
• The Speaker’s role is crucial in maintaining order and ensuring the rules of the Lok Sabha are followed during the Joint Sitting.
 
 
 
• **Historical Instances of Joint Sitting:**
 
 
• The first Joint Sitting was held in 1961 to pass the Dowry Prohibition Bill, 1959, which had faced disagreements between the two Houses.
 
• Another notable Joint Sitting was held in 2002 to pass the Prevention of Terrorism Act (POTA), which had been a contentious issue between the Houses.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Joint Sitting:**
 
 
• It is a unique provision in India’s bicameral legislature, designed to prevent legislative paralysis.
 
• The decision in a Joint Sitting is taken by a majority vote of the members present and voting, ensuring equal participation of both Houses.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the Additional Director General (ADG) of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) in August 2024?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sanjeev Raina** was appointed as the Additional Director General (ADG) of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) in August 2024.
 
• ITBP is a Central Armed Police Force (CAPF) of India that was established primarily to guard the borders between India and Tibet.
 
• The ADG rank is one of the senior-most positions in the ITBP, responsible for overseeing and ensuring operational efficiency and strategic deployment of forces. *Hence, option 1 is correct.*
 
• Sanjeev Raina is a seasoned officer with extensive experience in paramilitary forces and has held various critical positions before this appointment.
 
• The appointment of senior officers in ITBP is crucial, given its strategic role in securing the nation's borders and managing operations in high-altitude terrains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP):**

 
 
• ITBP was established in 1962 after the Sino-Indian War to guard the Indo-China border along the Himalayan region.
 
• It operates under the Ministry of Home Affairs and is responsible for border security, disaster response, and anti-Naxal operations.
 
• ITBP personnel are specially trained to operate in high-altitude regions and extreme climatic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Role of Additional Director General (ADG):**

• The role involves coordinating with state and central agencies for border management and law enforcement.
 
• ADG plays a strategic role in modernizing the force and implementing advanced technologies for better surveillance.
 
 
 
• **India-China Border:**

• This region includes difficult terrains like Ladakh, Arunachal Pradesh, and Sikkim, making ITBP's role vital in securing national sovereignty.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Border Security:**
 
 
• The rugged terrain and harsh climate conditions demand specialized training and equipment for personnel.
 
• Frequent tensions along the LAC require constant vigilance and preparedness to handle conflicts diplomatically and tactically.

questions.question: Which group of people settled in northwestern India around Taxila in the 1st century BC?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kushanas**, a Central Asian nomadic group, settled in northwestern India around Taxila during the 1st century BC.
 
• The Kushanas were known for their significant contributions to the cultural and political landscape of the Indian subcontinent, including the spread of Buddhism.
 
• They established the Kushana Empire, which stretched across present-day Afghanistan, Pakistan, and northern India, with Taxila as a major cultural and trade hub.
 
• Taxila became a renowned centre for education, trade, and Buddhist learning under the Kushana rule.
 
• The Kushanas were instrumental in promoting cross-cultural exchanges between Central Asia, China, and India, influencing art, religion, and trade routes like the Silk Road.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kushana Empire:**

 
 
• The Kushanas were originally part of the Yuezhi tribe, a nomadic group displaced from China and Central Asia.
 
• Their empire was established by Kujula Kadphises, with later rulers like Kanishka expanding its boundaries and influence.
 
 
 
• **Taxila:**
 
 
• Taxila was an ancient city located in present-day Pakistan and served as a major educational and cultural centre during ancient times.
 
• Under the Kushanas, Taxila flourished as a hub of Buddhist learning, attracting scholars, traders, and pilgrims from various regions.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism and Art:**
 
 
• The Kushanas played a significant role in the spread of Buddhism to Central Asia and China, with Kanishka being a notable patron of the religion.
 
• The Kushan ruler who convened the **Fourth Buddhist Council** was **Kanishka**. This council was held in **Kashmir **around the **1st century CE **under his patronage to resolve disputes and compile Buddhist teachings. It was during this council that the Mahayana school of Buddhism gained prominence, and the texts were translated from Pali to Sanskrit. 
 
• The Gandhara art style, combining Indian and Greco-Roman influences, flourished during the Kushana period, especially in regions like Taxila.
 
 
 
• **Silk Road Influence:**
 
 
• The Kushana Empire was strategically located along the Silk Road, facilitating trade and cultural exchanges between East and West.
 
• Their rule contributed to the economic prosperity of regions like Taxila, making it a key node in ancient trade networks.

questions.question: What is the process of ocean acidification?

options.text: Decrease in pH due to carbon dioxide absorption

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ocean acidification** is the ongoing decrease in the pH of the Earth's oceans caused by the absorption of atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO₂).
 
• When CO₂ dissolves in seawater, it reacts with water to form carbonic acid (H₂CO₃), which then dissociates into bicarbonate (HCO₃⁻) and hydrogen ions (H⁺).
 
• The increase in hydrogen ions (H⁺) lowers the pH of seawater, making it more acidic. *This is why the correct answer is statement 2.*
 
• Ocean acidification has significant impacts on marine ecosystems, particularly on organisms like corals, shellfish, and plankton that rely on calcium carbonate for their shells and skeletons.
 
• Since the industrial revolution, ocean pH has dropped by approximately 0.1 units, representing a 30% increase in acidity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Process of Ocean Acidification:**

 
 
• Carbon dioxide (CO₂) from human activities, such as burning fossil fuels and deforestation, is released into the atmosphere.
 
• Approximately 25-30% of this CO₂ is absorbed by the oceans, where it reacts with seawater to form carbonic acid.
 
• Carbonic acid dissociates into bicarbonate ions and hydrogen ions, increasing the acidity of ocean water.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Marine Life:**
 
 
• Marine organisms such as corals and mollusks, which depend on calcium carbonate for their shells and skeletons, are particularly vulnerable as acidification reduces the availability of carbonate ions.
 
• Reduced calcification rates in these organisms can lead to weaker structures and disrupt marine food chains.
 
 
 
• **pH Scale and Ocean Chemistry:**
 
 
• The pH scale measures the acidity or alkalinity of a solution. A decrease in pH indicates an increase in acidity.
 
• Pre-industrial ocean pH was approximately 8.2, but current levels have dropped to about 8.1, which may seem small but represents a significant chemical change.
 
 
 
• **Global Implications of Ocean Acidification:**
 
 
• It threatens marine biodiversity and ecosystems, particularly coral reefs, which are vital for coastal protection and fisheries.
 
• Ocean acidification also has socioeconomic impacts, as it affects fisheries, aquaculture, and tourism sectors that rely on healthy marine ecosystems.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers on the cheque should be noted to check its status?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cheque number**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cheque number:** This unique identification number is present on every cheque and helps in tracking and verifying the status of the cheque.
 
• The cheque number is printed at the bottom-left corner of the cheque and is essential for identifying specific cheques during banking transactions.
 
• Banks use the cheque number to check whether a cheque has been cleared, is pending, or has been canceled or bounced. *Hence, this is the correct option.*
 
• The cheque number is linked to an account holder and is stored in banking systems to ensure accurate tracking of transactions.
 
• It plays a vital role in preventing fraud, as duplicate or fake cheques can be identified by their number.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic Ink Character Recognition (MICR):**

 
 
• MICR is a technology used in banking to read and process cheques. It encodes information such as the bank branch, account number, and cheque number using magnetic ink.
 
• While MICR is crucial for automated processing, it does not directly help in tracking the status of a cheque. It is primarily used for sorting and processing cheques faster.
 
 
 
• **Indian Financial System Code (IFSC):**
 
 
• IFSC is an alphanumeric code used for identifying bank branches during electronic fund transfers like NEFT, RTGS, and IMPS.
 
• It is printed on cheques but does not provide information about the status of a cheque.
 
 
 
• **Other components on a cheque:**
 
 
• Details like date, payee name, amount, and signature are essential for cheque validation but are not used to track its status.
 
• The cheque number remains the most reliable identifier for checking its status or history.

questions.question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the 141st International Olympic Committee (IOC) Session in which of the following cities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** inaugurated the 141st International Olympic Committee (IOC) Session in **Mumbai** on October 15, 2023.
 
• The IOC Session is a significant event where members of the International Olympic Committee make critical decisions regarding the Olympic Games and sports development globally.
 
• Mumbai was selected as the host city for this IOC Session after India won the bid in 2022 during the 139th IOC Session held in Beijing.
 
• This marked the first IOC Session held in India in over four decades; the last session was hosted in New Delhi in 1983.
 
• The event reinforced India’s commitment to promoting sports and its aspirations to host the Olympic Games in the future.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Olympic Committee (IOC):**

 
 
• The IOC is a Switzerland-based organization that oversees the Olympic Movement and ensures the organization of the Olympic Games.
 
• Founded in 1894, the IOC works with National Olympic Committees (NOCs) and international sports federations to promote sports worldwide.
 
 
 
• **IOC Sessions:**
 
 
• IOC Sessions are annual or extraordinary meetings where key decisions related to the Olympic Games are discussed and voted upon.
 
• These sessions cover topics such as host city selection for upcoming Games, policy changes, and updates on sports development programs.
 
 
 
• **India’s Role in Global Sports:**
 
 
• India has been actively working to enhance its global sports profile, hosting events such as the Commonwealth Games and bidding for future Olympic Games.
 
• The IOC Session in Mumbai has further strengthened India’s position as a global sports hub and its readiness to host international events.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the IOC Session in Mumbai:**

questions.question: Which Indian labour law and social security measure aims to guarantee the 'right to work'?

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
The Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA):** Enacted in 2005, it aims to enhance the livelihood security of rural households in India by providing at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year to every rural household.
 
• MGNREGA is a demand-driven law, meaning that work is provided upon request by eligible rural households. This ensures that the "right to work" is upheld as a legal guarantee.
 
• Under MGNREGA, unskilled manual labor is provided for public works projects, including water conservation, afforestation, and rural infrastructure development.
 
• The Act empowers local institutions like Gram Panchayats to plan and implement projects, ensuring community participation and transparency.
 
• MGNREGA mandates timely wage payments and promotes gender equity by ensuring equal wages for men and women. *Hence, option 1 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Features of MGNREGA:**

 
 
• The Act provides a legal guarantee for wage employment, making it unique among welfare schemes globally. If employment is not provided within 15 days of application, the applicant is entitled to an unemployment allowance.
 
• The types of work permissible under MGNREGA focus on sustainable development, such as construction of check dams, rural roads, and irrigation canals.
 
• Social audits are conducted to ensure transparency and accountability in the implementation of MGNREGA projects.
 
 
 
• **Significance of MGNREGA:**
 
 
• It has contributed significantly to poverty reduction, rural development, and empowerment of marginalized communities.
 
• The program provides a critical safety net during economic crises, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, when rural employment opportunities were severely impacted.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Implementation:**
 
 
• Delays in wage payments and inadequate funding have been persistent issues, affecting the program’s efficiency and credibility.
 
• Instances of corruption, including fake job cards and misappropriation of funds, have been reported in some areas.
 
• Despite its challenges, MGNREGA remains a cornerstone of India’s social security framework.
